A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe CoMOGA by the same authors. Both main texts and all appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original simulation results on Safety Gymnasium, legged locomotion and MO-Gymnasium, including reward-scaling and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: Section 6 and the appendices report original benchmark results, learning curves, a CAGrad comparison and constrained toy-optimization trajectories.

M1.justification: While retaining objective-to-constraint conversion, v2 removes the formal active-constraint filtering and K/G-dependent margin and scaling construction, and introduces a normalized dual-weight update with new clipping parameters in Equation (10). Algorithm 1 also samples trajectory/preference pairs from replay instead of fresh preferences. These revise the specified procedure, although v1 already disabled the K/G corrections in its main experiments.

E1.justification: Safety Gymnasium and the biped/quadruped tasks remain. The unconstrained benchmark changes from four tasks to six: Half-Cheetah and Hopper remain; Water-Reservoir and Lunar-Lander are removed; Humanoid, Ant, Walker2d and Swimmer are added. V2 also evaluates a constrained toy-optimization problem in Appendix A.

E2.justification: The main RL comparators CAPQL, PD-MORL and LP3 are retained. V2 adds CAGrad+Lagrangian comparisons in both legged locomotion tasks in Section 6.5 and Figure 7. Linear scalarization appears in both versions, but in different diagnostic experiments.

E3.justification: V1 Tables 6–7 and v2 Tables 4–5 report CoMOGA preference samples changing from 3 to 10 for constrained tasks, and its unconstrained-task policy learning rate changing from 3e-5 to 3e-4 and local-region size from 0.1 to 0.05. The new toy experiment uses four fixed initial points and preference (0.5, 0.5). Hypervolume and normalized-sparsity definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's reward-scaling comparison and sensitivity studies over local-region size, K and G are removed, rather than relocated. V2 instead tests whether combining CAGrad with Lagrangian constraint handling is sufficient, and adds a toy study illustrating initialization-dependent failures of linear scalarization. The supplementary evidence addresses substantially different questions.

E5.justification: V1 reports five-seed means and individual-seed Pareto fronts. V2 adds learning-curve variability bands, explicitly defined in Figure 4 as one-quarter of the standard deviation across five seeds. The reported seed count does not increase, and no significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds training trajectories, results for four additional MuJoCo tasks, CAGrad and toy-example outcomes, and training times, while removing dropped-task and sensitivity-study results. Reported Safety Gymnasium rankings also change: v1 Table 1 has LP3 leading Single-Point-Goal hypervolume, whereas v2 Figure 5 reports CoMOGA leading all four tasks. Revised settings prevent treating this as a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: V1's stepwise feasibility and epsilon-CP-stationarity analysis under smoothness and convex-constraint assumptions is replaced by tabular natural-policy-gradient theorems using Slater and Robbins-Monro conditions. V2 provides a generalized update theorem and a modified-CoMOGA convergence theorem with new proofs in Appendix B, and adds a formal gradient-conflict definition. The basic transformation argument is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift the central contribution from scale invariance to avoiding gradient conflicts and undesirable local optima. The convergence claim changes from local Pareto optimality to CP optimality under explicitly tabular conditions. Handling constraints without additional optimization variables remains a central claim.

C2.justification: V2 interprets performance on bipedal, hopper and humanoid tasks through gradient conflicts and unstable dynamics, replacing much of v1's scale-sensitivity explanation. It also offers a reward-design explanation for Walker2d results. Section 7 newly acknowledges that preventing objective decreases can restrict Pareto-front coverage and proposes relaxing conflict avoidance.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix C.3 newly reports Intel Xeon E5-2680 and NVIDIA TITAN Xp hardware and per-method training times in Table 2. Section 5 documents critic losses and target options, including Retrace. Network architectures and most task details are retained, while v1's detailed dual-QP implementation appendix is condensed into the main method discussion.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from a scale-invariant alternative to scalarization and MOMPO toward applying conflict-averse multi-task-learning ideas to CMORL. CAGrad, already cited in v1, becomes central; v2 adds gradient-surgery and tabular policy-gradient references. The COptiDICE discussion and the separate dual-method category in constrained RL are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Transformation receives its own subsection, locomotion experiments precede Safety Gymnasium, and the conclusion incorporates limitations. The appendices are reorganized around a new toy example, replacement proofs, experimental details and front visualizations.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Endpoint benchmark tables are replaced by grids of learning curves with variability bands; toy-example figures and a timing table are added; scaling and sensitivity displays are removed. The combined appendix Pareto-front figure is reorganized into separate, enlarged figures by task family, and the method diagram is revised.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical transparency through learning curves, variability reporting, resource details and an explicit coverage limitation. However, it removes v1's scale and hyperparameter robustness evidence. The replacement convergence claim also has unresolved support: Appendix B.3 uses policy convergence to establish the weight-convergence condition needed by its convergence theorem. These benefits, losses and uncertainty about a central theoretical contribution prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
